items.prompt:
Read.

I opened the door and my heart pounded.

This is:
A) first person
B) third person
C) no narrator

Read.

She opened the door and her heart pounded.

This is:
A) first person
B) third person
C) a poem

First-person narration uses the words:
A) I and we
B) he and she
C) it and they

'They climbed the hill together.' This is:
A) first person
B) third person
C) second person

Which point of view lets the narrator share their OWN thoughts directly?
A) first person
B) third person
C) neither

steps: 'I' shares the narrator's thoughts. Key is A.

items.prompt:
To rewrite 'He was afraid' in first person, you would write:
A) I was afraid
B) They were afraid
C) She was afraid

steps: He to I. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Read.

Maria watched the storm. She wondered if the ship would make it home.

The narration is:
A) first person (a character telling it with 'I')
B) third person (an outside narrator using 'she')
C) a play script
items.answer: B) third person (an outside narrator using 'she')

steps: Uses 'she,' outside narrator. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) third person (an outside narrator using 'she')

items.prompt:
What is one difference between first- and third-person narration?
A) First person uses 'I' and shares one character's view; third person uses 'he/she' from outside
B) They are exactly the same
C) Only third person is a story
items.answer: A) First person uses 'I' and shares one character's view; third person uses 'he/she' from outside

solution.answer: A) First person uses 'I' and shares one character's view; third person uses 'he/she' from outside
